main.description: Format-neutral meaning of a hazard notice: CAP 1.2 category, severity, urgency, certainty and response types, plus onset time and regional scales. The affected area is geo#area and the valid period is validity; neither is repeated here. Anyone can sign this extension, so receivers distinguish verified public information from user claims before alert-style display.

status.description: CAP status: Actual, Exercise or Test. Required so that an omission is never read as a real event.

category.description: CAP 1.2 category values. The coarse fallback classification; the kind of hazard is given by a dev.jisaku.mosimo.hazard.* extension.

severity.description: CAP 1.2 severity. Unknown values are treated as Unknown.

urgency.description: CAP 1.2 urgency. An all-clear uses Past.

responseTypes.description: CAP 1.2 responseType values. Omit when the source gives no action. AllClear marks the end of the threat, not the retraction of an erroneous notice.

onset.description: When the phenomenon began or is expected to begin (CAP onset; earthquake origin time). UTC with an uppercase Z suffix. Omit when unknown; never fill from the issue, receipt or creation time.

event.description: The notice's own name in the source, for display only.

scales.description: Regional scales kept verbatim (seismic intensity, warning level, ...). At most one entry per scheme.

glide.description: An issued GLIDE number, e.g. EQ-2011-000028-JPN.

scale.description: A value on a regional or international scale, kept in its original notation.

scheme.description: Registered scale name, e.g. jp.jma.shindo, jp.jma.warning-level, intl.mmi, or a reversed domain owned by its definer.

value.description: The value in the scale's own notation, e.g. 5+ for JMA seismic intensity 5 upper.

basis.description: Whether the value is observed or forecast. Omit when unknown.
